workflow.critical: NEVER display passwords in plain text — always mask as ****
Execute ALL steps in exact order

step.goal: Resolve suite name from argument or active suite in test-suites.yml

check.if: no suite name argument is provided
file does not exist or active_suite is empty
check.output: ❌ No active suite found. Run /aiqa-analyzestory --suite <name> first.

step.action: Find the suite entry where name = {suite_name}

check.output: ⚠️ Suite status is "{current_status}" — test data may not have been generated yet. Continuing validation; artifact checks will catch missing files.

step.goal: Load test data files and spec for cross-reference
step.action: Record expected file paths: - Valid: {output_folder}/{story_id}/test-data/{suite_name}-valid.json - Edge: {output_folder}/{story_id}/test-data/{suite_name}-edge.json - Security: {output_folder}/{story_id}/test-data/{suite_name}-security.json
If each file exists: read it and attempt JSON parse; record parse errors
Read config.yaml to load {test_users} for credential verification
If spec file exists ({output_folder}/{story_id}/e2e/tests/{suite_name}.spec.js): read it to extract the field names used in testData references

step.goal: Run all quality checks and collect issues
step.check: All 3 JSON data files exist at the correct paths inside {output_folder}/{story_id}/test-data/
All 3 JSON files are valid parseable JSON — no trailing commas, no unquoted keys, no syntax errors
valid.json includes user credentials sourced from {test_users} in config.yaml — NOT invented or hardcoded; verify by comparing usernames to config.yaml test_users list
Field names in the JSON files match the actual form fields / API request keys used in the spec file — no mismatched or missing keys
valid.json contains realistic positive data matching the story's domain — no generic "test123", "foo", "bar", or "test@test.com" placeholders
edge.json covers: empty strings, null values, maximum-length strings, special characters (؟!@#), numeric boundaries, zero, negative numbers
security.json contains: SQL injection payloads (' OR '1'='1), XSS payloads (<script>alert(1)</script>), CSRF tokens, oversized inputs
Expected success/error messages in the JSON match what the application actually returns — not invented strings (ask user if uncertain)

step.goal: Present validation report and ask how to proceed

check.output:
✅ Validation Passed — /aiqa-generatetestdata
All 8 quality checks passed. Test data files are correct and complete. Suite: {suite_name} No issues found — safe to proceed to /aiqa-runtests.

step.output:
╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗ ║ 🔍 Validation Report — /aiqa-generatetestdata ║ ╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
Suite : {suite_name} Output : {output_folder}/{story_id}/test-data/
🔴 Critical ({critical_count}): (for each Critical issue: " • {id} — {description}" + detail) (if none: " None")
🟠 High ({high_count}): (for each High issue: " • {id} — {description}" + detail) (if none: " None")
🟡 Medium ({medium_count}): (for each Medium issue: " • {id} — {description}") (if none: " None")
🔵 Low ({low_count}): (for each Low issue: " • {id} — {description}") (if none: " None")
Total issues: {total_issues}
step.ask: How would you like to proceed? A) Fix ALL {total_issues} issue(s) — resolve every finding B) Fix only Critical + High ({critical_count + high_count} issue(s)) — skip Medium and Low C) Skip — keep the report, apply no fixes

step.goal: Apply fixes to test data JSON files
step.action: Determine issues to fix: Choice A → fix ALL issues Choice B → fix only Critical and High issues

For each issue selected for fixing: TD-1 → re-run /aiqa-generatetestdata {suite_name} to create missing files TD-2 → replace generic placeholder values (test123, foo, test@test.com) with domain-specific realistic values derived from the user story context TD-3 → load credentials from config.yaml test_users; update valid.json with the actual username(s) and masked password reference; NEVER display passwords in plain text TD-4 → add missing edge cases to edge.json: empty string for each field, null values, 256+ character string, special chars (؟!@#$%), zero and negative numbers TD-5 → add missing security payloads to security.json: SQL injection (' OR '1'='1--), XSS (<script>alert(1)</script>), oversized input (10,000 chars) TD-6 → fix JSON syntax errors: remove trailing commas, quote all keys, balance braces/brackets; validate parse after fix TD-7 → cross-reference field names with the spec file; rename any mismatched keys; add any missing keys that the spec references TD-8 → ask user: "What does the application return on success/error?" then update expectedMessages accordingly Save all corrected files to disk.
step.output: ✍️ Fixes applied — test data files updated.

step.goal: Re-verify fixed checks and report final status
step.action: Re-run ONLY the checks that were targeted for fixing
step.output:
📋 Validation Summary — /aiqa-generatetestdata
(for each fixed check:) ✅ {id} — resolved: {what was corrected} (for each still failing:) ❌ {id} — still failing: {reason} (for each skipped check:) ⏭️ {id} — skipped (outside selected fix scope)
(if all targeted checks pass:) ✅ All targeted issues resolved. Safe to proceed to /aiqa-runtests.
(if some still fail:) ⚠️ {remaining} issue(s) could not be fixed automatically. Edit the data files manually, then re-run /aiqa-generatetestdata-validate.
